entities.summary: Shams al-Din Ildeniz, Eldigüz or Shamseddin Eldeniz was a prominent atabeg of the Seljuq empire and founder of the dynasty of Eldiguzids, atabegs of Azerbaijan, which held sway over Armenia, Iranian Azerbaijan, and most of northwestern Persia from the second half of the 12th century to the early decades of the 13th. Ildeniz played a crucial role in the politics of the region, navigating the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various Turkic and Persian factions. He successfully expanded the Eldiguzid empire, absorbing territories from the neighboring Kurdish and Georgian states. Ildeniz's military campaigns were marked by strategic victories, including the capture of the strategic city of Nakhchivan from the Georgian Kingdom. His diplomatic efforts also earned him the respect of the Seljuq sultan, who recognized Ildeniz as a key ally in the region. Ildeniz's legacy extended beyond his military and diplomatic achievements, as he also patronized the arts and architecture, commissioning numerous buildings and monuments throughout his territories. He was particularly known for his support of the famous Seljuq poet, Nizami Ganjavi, who would go on to become a celebrated figure in Persian literature. Ildeniz's impact on the region was significant, as he helped to establish the Eldiguzid dynasty as a major power in the region, paving the way for the rise of the Mongols in the late 13th century. His reign also saw the beginning of the decline of the Georgian Kingdom, as the Eldiguzids gradually absorbed their territories. Ildeniz's remarkable life and achievements make him a fascinating figure in the history of the Middle East, and his legacy continues to be felt in the modern-day cultures and traditions of the region.
